rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa argues that once the offering reaches the Kaaba it qualifies as an offering reaching it, discharging the duty.
rows.anchor: أنها لما وصلت إلى الكعبة فقد صارت هديا بالغ الكعبة ، فوجب أن يخرج عن العهدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi and Ibn Amir read the phrase as an annexation, while the other readers use nominative tanwin for kafara and nominative unmarked food.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر { أو كفارة طعام } على إضافة الكفارة إلى الطعام ، والباقون { أو كفارة } بالرفع والتنوين طعام بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The annexation is apt because the person is offered a choice among sacrifice, fasting, and food, so the expiation is specified as food rather than sacrifice or fasting.
rows.anchor: لما خير المكلف بين ثلاثة أشياء : الهدي ، والصيام ، والطعام ، حسنت الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the other reading, food is appositional clarification of the penalty, since it is the expiation for killing game rather than an expiation belonging to food.
rows.anchor: عطف على قوله { فجزاء } و { طعام مساكين } عطف بيان ، لأن الطعام هو الكفارة

rows.speaker: الشافعي ومالك وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i, Malik, and Abu Hanifa hold that “or” gives the offender a choice among the alternatives.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي ومالك وأبو حنيفة رحمهم الله : كلمة { أو } في هذه الآية للتخيير

rows.speaker: أحمد وزفر
rows.claim: Ahmad and Zufar understand “or” as ordering the alternatives; they argue that the word can mark non-choice and that the threat language makes the penalty severe.
rows.anchor: وقال أحمد وزفر : إنها للترتيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that paying an equivalent is no harsher than paying food, so choice does not undermine the severity of requiring an equivalent penalty.
rows.anchor: والجواب : أن إخراج المثل ليس أقوى عقوبة من إخراج الطعام ، فالتخيير لا يقدح في القدر الحاصل من العقوبة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: For game with a livestock equivalent, al-Shafi'i gives three choices: provide that equivalent, buy and give food for its value, or fast.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي رحمه الله : هو مخير بين ثلاثة أشياء : إن شاء أخرج المثل ، وإن شاء قوم المثل بدراهم

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: For game without a livestock equivalent, al-Shafi'i gives two choices: value the game to buy food for charity, or fast.
rows.anchor: وأما الصيد الذي لا مثل له ، فهو مخير فيه بين شيئين ، بين أن يقوم الصيد بالدراهم ويشتري بتلك الدراهم طعاما

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i values the food by the livestock equivalent because that equivalent is the penalty; he also says valuing the equivalent is more exact than valuing the game itself.
rows.anchor: المثل من النعم هو الجزاء والطعام بناء عليه فيعدل به كما يعدل عن الصوم بالطعام

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومالك
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa and Malik calculate food by the value of the animal killed; Abu Hanifa argues that an equivalent for a destroyed item should be measured by that item when possible.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة ومالك رحمهما الله : إنما يشتري الطعام بقيمته

rows.speaker: أكثر الفقهاء
rows.claim: Most jurists value the game in the place where it was killed.
rows.anchor: فقال أكثر الفقهاء : إنما يقوم في المكان الذي قتل الصيد فيه

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi values the game in Mecca at Meccan prices because the expiation is performed there.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي : يقوم بمكة بثمن مكة لأنه يكفر بها

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra distinguishes ʿadl as an equal from a different kind and ʿidl as an equivalent of the same kind, illustrated by matching a servant or sheep.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : العدل ما عادل الشيء من غير جنسه ، والعدل المثل

rows.speaker: أبو الهيثم
rows.claim: Abu al-Haytham says ʿadl means an equivalent and ʿidl means value, also describing a balanced load and valuation across kinds.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الهيثم : العدل المثل ، والعدل القيمة ، والعدل اسم حمل معدول بحمل آخر

rows.speaker: الزجاج وابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj and Ibn al-A'rabi treat the two forms as synonymous.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج وابن الأعرابي : العدل والعدل سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative in “fasting” is a specification (tamyiz), as in saying two pounds of honey; an omitted “of” is understood.
rows.anchor: وقوله { صياما } نصب على التمييز ، كنا تقول عندي رطلان عسلا

rows.speaker: الشافعي وعطاء
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i and Ata require one day of fasting per mudd of food.
rows.anchor: مذهب الشافعي رضي الله عنه : أنه يصوم لكل مد يوما وهو قول عطاء

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa requires one day of fasting per half-saʿ of food.
rows.anchor: مذهب أبي حنيفة رحمه الله أنه يصوم لكل نصف صاع يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both schools measure fasting by one day's food; they differ because al-Shafi'i measures a day's food as a mudd and Abu Hanifa as half a saʿ.
rows.anchor: توافقا على أن الصوم مقدر بطعام يوم ، إلا أن طعام اليوم عند الشافعي مقدر بالمد ، وعند أبي حنيفة رحمه الله مقدر بنصف صاع

rows.speaker: جمهور الفقهاء
rows.claim: Most jurists say the game-killer chooses which of the three alternatives to perform, since the verse makes one of them obligatory by choice.
rows.anchor: زعم جمهور الفقهاء أن الخيار في تعيين أحد هذه الثلاثة إلى قاتل الصيد

rows.speaker: محمد بن الحسن
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan assigns the choice among alternatives to the two arbiters, based on the verse assigning judgment to them.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن الحسن رحمه الله إلى الحكمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the arbiters determine the livestock equivalent, by its value or physical form; they do not choose among food, fasting, and sacrifice.
rows.anchor: وأما الاذي يحكم به ذوا عدل فهو تعيين المثل ، إما في القيمة أو في الخلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wabal denotes heaviness and unpleasantness; the Qur'anic phrase “a severe seizure” uses it in the sense of something heavy.
rows.anchor: الوبال في اللغة : عبارة عما فيه من الثقل والمكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The penalty is called wabal because two options diminish wealth and fasting pains the body; all are burdensome and deter hunting in the sanctuary or during consecration.
rows.anchor: اثنان منها توجب تنقيص المال ، وهو ثقيل على الطبع ، وهما الجزاء بالمثل والاطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that God forgave what occurred in pre-Islamic times and before the prohibition in Islam.
rows.anchor: عفا الله عما مضى في الجاهلية وعما سلف قبل التحريم في الإسلام

rows.speaker: من لا يوجب الجزاء إلا في المرة الأولى
rows.claim: A second view imposes expiation only for the first offense: after a repeat offense, God's punishment suffices and no further expiation is due; its argument treats the consequence clause as a sufficient recompense.
rows.anchor: وهو قول من لا يوجب الجزاء إلا في المرة الأولى

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh analyzes the conditional clauses as omitting a subject pronoun before the predicate, explaining why the prefixed fa is needed; he gives parallels in 2:126 and 72:13.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه في قوله { ومن عاد فينتقم الله منه } وفي قوله { ومن كفر فأمتعه قليلا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God comforts the Messenger and warns the people to travel and inspect the traces of earlier peoples destroyed for rejecting messengers, strengthening reflection and insight.
rows.anchor: لتعرفوا صحة ما أخبركم الرسول عنه من نزول العذاب على الذين كذبوا الرسل في الأزمنة السالفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Then look” permits travel for trade and other benefits while requiring reflection on the ruins; by contrast, “so look” makes looking the purpose of travel, as in 3:137.
rows.anchor: قوله { فانظروا } يدل على أنه تعالى جعل النظر سببا عن السير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes the Creator, resurrection, and prophecy: contingent bodies and qualities imply a chooser who specifies them; enduring knowledge and power permit recreation; a sovereign who commands needs a messenger.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية وافية بإثبات هذه المطالب الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question followed by its answer suits a truth so evident that none can deny it, since the signs of contingency are manifest in bodies and their qualities.
rows.anchor: إنما يحسن في الموضع الذي يكون الجواب قد بلغ في الظهور إلى حيث لا يقدر على إنكاره منكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people already acknowledged that God created the heavens and earth; Razi cites this acknowledgment to show that God's ownership and power were familiar to them.
rows.anchor: ولئن سألتهم من خلق * السماوات والارض ليقولن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's self-imposed mercy means that He continually bestows blessings and promises future blessing, imposing it on Himself as grace and generosity.
rows.anchor: بل أبدا ينعم وأبدا يعد في المستقبل بالإنعام ومع ذلك فقد كتب على نفسه ذلك وأوجبه إيجاب الفضل والكرم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the mercy is God's giving people a lifetime of respite, withholding total destruction, and not hastening punishment in this world.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم : تلك الرحمة هي أنه تعالى يمهلهم مدة عمرهم ويرفع عنهم عذاب الاستئصال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation limits the promised mercy to those who stop denying the messengers, repent, believe them, and accept their law.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن المراد أنه كتب على نفسه الرحمة لمن ترك التكذيب بالرسل وتاب وأناب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet reports that after completing creation God wrote that His mercy preceded His wrath.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( لما فرغ الله من الخلق كتب كتابا أن رحمتي سبقت غضبي )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers the objection that precedence would make divine will temporal by saying the report means precedence in abundance, not in time.
rows.anchor: المراد بهذا السبق سبق الكثرة لا سبق الزمان

rows.speaker: سلمان
rows.claim: Salman reports that God created one hundred mercies, kept ninety-nine, and distributed one among creatures, through which they show compassion; at the end the mercy is reserved for the pious.
rows.anchor: وعن سلمان أنه تعالى لما خلق السماء والأرض خلق مائة رحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in “He will surely gather you” is the lām of an implicit oath: “By God, He will surely gather you.”
rows.anchor: الأول : ( اللام ) في قوله { ليجمعنكم } لام قسم مضمر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view makes the gathering clause independent: mercy is respite in this life, while gathering means later resurrection and accounting for every deed.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم أنه كلام مبتدأ ،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view connects the clause to the preceding statement: God wrote mercy upon Himself and wrote that He would gather people on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : أنع متعلق بما قبله والتقدير : كتب ربكم على نفسه الرحمة .

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third reading treats the gathering as an explanation of mercy, since fear of Judgment Day prevents social disorder and is itself a great worldly mercy.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أنه لما قال : { كتب ربكم على نفسه الرحمة } فكأنه قيل : وما تلك الرحمة ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from third-person report to direct address intensifies the threat: a wise sovereign does not neglect subjects or equate obedience with disobedience, so He will gather and judge them.
rows.anchor: والمقصود منه التأكيد في التهديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Four explanations are given for “to the Day”: the preposition is extra, means “in,” conceals the gathering place, or describes successive generations continuing until the Day.
rows.anchor: أن كلمة { إلى } في قوله { إلى يوم القيامة } فيها أقوال : الأول : أنها صلة

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash parses “those who lost themselves” as an accusative appositive to the pronoun in “gather you,” meaning God gathers these idolaters.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الأخفش

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses the phrase as a nominative subject with “they do not believe” as its predicate; the fa marks a condition-result relation, as in the example about the one who honors me.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الزجاج ، أن قوله { الذين خسروا أنفسهم } رفع بالابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the wording seems to make loss cause disbelief, Razi says prior divine decree of loss and abandonment caused their refusal to believe, which is the Sunni doctrine.
rows.anchor: سبق القضاء بالخسران والخذلان ، هو الذي حملهم على الامتناع من الايمان ، وذلك عين مذهب أهل السنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If idolaters turn to God rather than idols in hardship, worship of powerless idols is irrational; the argument works only if proof and reasoning are accepted, making the passage evidence that religion rests on proof rather than blind imitation.
rows.anchor: إذا كنتم ترجعون عند نزول الشدائد إلى الله تعالى لا إلى الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some people turn to God in hardship, while others remain in disbelief even under affliction; Razi says this shows that without God's guidance people will not be guided, whether they witness terrifying signs or not.
rows.anchor: وذلك يدل على مذهبنا من أن الله تعالى إذا لم يهده لم يهتد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse omits the understood words “messengers, whom they opposed,” before saying God seized the earlier communities.
rows.anchor: في الآية محذوف والتقدير : ولقد أرسلنا إلى أمم من قبلك رسلا فخالفوهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan glosses al-ba'sa as severe poverty and al-darra as illnesses and pains.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن ( البأساء ) شدة الفقر من البؤس ( والضراء ) الأمراض والأوجاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers and hardships were sent so people would humble themselves; tadarruʿ means submission and abandoning rebellion, from a root meaning abasement, and this history consoles the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ومعنى التضرع التخشع وهو عبارة عن الانقياد وترك التمرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier people who called to God sought relief from affliction but did not call with sincere devotion; alternatively, they were a different group from those described here.
rows.anchor: أولئك أقوام ، وهؤلاء أقوام آخرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “If only” negates their supplication: they did not beseech God when affliction came, and their only excuse was stubbornness, hardened hearts, and pride in Satan-adorned deeds.
rows.anchor: معناه نفي التضرع . والتقدير فلم يتضرعوا إذ جاءهم بأسنا

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i argues that “perhaps they would humble themselves” shows God sent messengers and afflictions intending all people to humble themselves and believe, so God wills faith and obedience for everyone.
rows.anchor: احتج الجبائي بقوله { لعلهم يتضرعون } فقال : هذا يدل على أنه تعالى إنما أرسل الرسل إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects al-Jubba'i's inference from laʿalla: hope or wishing cannot apply literally to God, and treating the phrase as an expressed purpose does not establish a divine motive governing His decree and will.
rows.anchor: كلمة ( لعل ) تفيد الترجي والتمني ؛ وذلك في حق الله تعالى محال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse instead shows that they failed to humble themselves because their hearts hardened and Satan adorned their deeds; if they caused their own hardness, the explanation regresses, while divine creation of it supports Razi's position.
rows.anchor: لأنها تدل على أنهم لم يتضرعوا لقسوة قلوبهم ولأجل أن الشيطان زين لهم أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Satan's adornment explains evil, asking why Satan persists creates another regress; ultimately motives arise in hearts by God's creation, which confirms Razi's doctrine and refutes his opponents.
rows.anchor: ثم ثبت أن تلك الدواعي لا تحصل إلا بإيجاد الله تعالى فحينئذ يصح قولنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God first tried them with hardship, then prosperity, as a caring father alternates severity and kindness for a child's good; when they rejoiced without gratitude or repentance, He seized them suddenly.
rows.anchor: وهذا كما يفعله الأب المشفق بولده يخاشنه تارة ويلاطفه أخرى طلبا لصلاحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening every door means opening every good formerly closed to them; they took the hardship as no punishment and the later blessings as deserved, revealing hardened hearts.
rows.anchor: فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء كان مغلقا عنهم من الخير

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that when God gives someone blessings despite disobedience, it is divine gradual entrapment (istidraj), then recites this verse.
rows.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا رأيت الله يعطي على المعاصي فإن ذلك استدراج من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The people of meaning say God seized them in comfort so their regret over losing safety and well-being would be greater.
rows.anchor: قال أهل المعاني : وإنما أخذوا في حال الرخاء والراحة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says mublis is one whose hope has ended, which explains calling a person silent after his argument runs out an “iblās.”
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : المبلس الذي انقطع رجاؤه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines mublis as intensely sorrowful and grieving; the broader language also covers despair of escape, loss of argument, and bewilderment at affliction.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : المبلس الشديد الحسرة الحزين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dabir is what follows a thing from behind, its last part; Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt's verse uses the term for a people whose end was cut off.
rows.anchor: الدابر التابع للشيء من خلفه كالولد للوالد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi cites the poetic line by Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt as an example of dabir describing a people whose end was cut off by punishment.
rows.anchor: فاستؤصلوا بعذاب حص دابرهم … فما استطاعوا له صرفا ولا انتصرا

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says dabir is the last person or part in a group.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة : دابر القوم آخرهم الذي يدبرهم

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asma'i says dabir means the root; cutting off a people's dabir means erasing their origin.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصمعي الدابر الأصل يقال قطع الله دابره أي أذهب الله أصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of praising God is that exterminating the wrongdoers was a great blessing to the messengers because it removed their harm.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى حمد نفسه على أن قطع دابرهم واستأصل شأفتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that their hardened hearts meant longer lives would bring more unbelief, sins, and deserved punishment, so ending their lives spared them further punishment.
rows.anchor: كلما ازدادت مدة حياتهم ازدادت أنواع كفرهم ومعاصيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation praises God's many prior favors: He imposed duties, removed excuses, tried them with hardship and ease, sent messengers, and finally cleansed the earth after they persisted in error.
rows.anchor: أخذهم أولا بالبأساء والضراء ، ثم نقلهم إلا الآلاء والنعماء
